name: Carl Friedrich Abel
description: Carl Friedrich Abel, a German viol player and composer, spent most of his career in London. There, together with Johann Christian Bach, he established a series of public concerts that helped shape the city's musical life. One of the last great virtuosos of the viola da gamba, he also wrote for keyboard, orchestra and chamber ensembles. His music reflects the transition from the Baroque idiom to the galant style.

name: John Adams
description: John Adams draws on the repetitive processes of minimalism while combining them with expansive orchestral writing and a dramatic sense of theatre inherited from opera. His works address American political history as well as intimate and mythological subjects. He has helped renew contemporary opera and American orchestral music.

name: Isaac Albéniz
description: The Catalan pianist and composer Isaac Albéniz helped renew Spanish music by bringing the rhythms, modes and colours of folk traditions into a pianistic language shaped by Liszt and French Romanticism. His best-known work, Iberia, turns the piano into an instrument of remarkable orchestral richness. He also wrote operas and numerous salon pieces, but his legacy rests above all on his mature works.

description: British composer, flautist and teacher William Alwyn wrote symphonies, concertos, operas and film scores. His style evolved from neoclassicism towards a freer, more chromatic idiom, underpinned by formidable orchestral craftsmanship. He was one of the most prolific film composers in Britain.

description: Louis Andriessen was a central figure in contemporary Dutch music. Breaking with Romantic and serial orchestral traditions, he forged an energetic, repetitive and politically engaged language shaped by jazz, Stravinsky and popular music. He often favoured unusual amplified ensembles, in which pulse and instrumental colour became structural forces. His influence on European new-music scenes was considerable.

description: Grażyna Bacewicz was a Polish composer and violinist whose work occupies a major place in 20th-century Central European music. Trained in Warsaw and Paris, she developed a language combining neoclassical clarity, rhythmic drive and increasingly adventurous harmonic exploration. Her dual career as performer and composer gave her instrumental writing an especially idiomatic character, notably in her concertos and chamber music.

name: Carl Philipp Emanuel Bach
description: The second son of Johann Sebastian Bach, Carl Philipp Emanuel Bach studied with [[bach|his father Johann Sebastian Bach]] before pursuing a career that took him from Berlin, where he served Frederick the Great, to Hamburg, where he succeeded Telemann as director of music. He became a leading exponent of the empfindsamer Stil, or sensitive style, with its emotional contrasts, unpredictable turns and almost improvisatory eloquence. His keyboard writing profoundly reshaped the sonata and influenced Haydn, Mozart and later generations. A respected theorist, he published an essential treatise on the art of keyboard playing. His aesthetic stands at the crossroads of the late Baroque and emerging Classical style.

description: The youngest son of [[bach|Johann Sebastian Bach]] first received his musical training within the family before travelling to Italy to study vocal music and opera. After converting to Catholicism, he became organist at Milan Cathedral and established himself as an opera composer. From 1762 he was based in London, where he gained an international reputation. His elegant, melodic and balanced style helped spread the galant taste and the emerging Classical idiom. He met the young [[mozart|Mozart]] in London in 1764 and had a significant influence on him, especially in the keyboard concerto.

name: Johann Sebastian Bach
description: Born into a Thuringian family of musicians, Johann Sebastian Bach worked as an organist and court musician before becoming cantor of St Thomas's Church in Leipzig in 1723. His activity was closely tied to the institutions that employed him: he wrote cantatas, Passions and motets for the liturgical calendar, as well as instrumental and chamber works. He absorbed German, Italian and French traditions and transformed them through extraordinary contrapuntal density. Long known mainly to specialists after his death, his music was rediscovered in the 19th century, notably through Mendelssohn, and became a central reference point for Western musical thought.

description: British guitarist Derek Bailey was a founding figure of European free improvisation. As co-founder of the Incus label, he helped build an independent international scene.

description: Béla Bartók was a composer, pianist and ethnomusicologist. Together with Zoltán Kodály, he collected and studied the folk music of Central and Eastern Europe, transforming its rhythms, modes and structures into a deeply personal modern language. His music combines rhythmic energy, formal rigour, timbral exploration and expressive power. He is one of the major composers of the 20th century, both for his quartets and for his orchestral and piano works.

name: François Bayle
description: François Bayle is a major composer of acousmatic music and one of the leading theorists of spatial listening. Born in Madagascar, he joined Pierre Schaeffer's Groupe de recherches musicales and developed the concept of the acousmonium, an orchestra of loudspeakers designed to perform works on fixed media. His music explores sonic images, imaginary spaces and transformations of perception. He made a profound contribution to the aesthetic autonomy of electroacoustic music.

name: Ludwig van Beethoven
description: Educated in Bonn and later based in Vienna, Ludwig van Beethoven first made his name as a pianist and improviser before becoming one of the most influential composers of his age. His music moves beyond the Classical inheritance of [[haydn|Haydn]] and [[mozart|Mozart]] and opens new paths towards Romanticism. His progressive deafness, profound by the beginning of the 19th century, transformed his life without stopping his creative work. His late sonatas, quartets and Missa solemnis explore forms of striking originality. The Ninth Symphony, with its choral finale, expands the ambitions of the symphonic genre.

description: Alban Berg brought together the Romantic inheritance and the radical language of atonality and later twelve-tone composition. A pupil of Schoenberg, he retained a lyrical and dramatic expressiveness that makes his music distinctive within the Second Viennese School. His two operas, Wozzeck and Lulu, are among the great works of 20th-century music theatre. His Violin Concerto, “To the Memory of an Angel”, has become one of the most frequently performed concertos of modernism.

Co-founder of the Studio di Fonologia in Milan, he explored electronics, collage, quotation and the transformation of the voice. His Sequenze form a laboratory of virtuosity and instrumental invention, while Sinfonia examines musical memory and the coexistence of multiple languages.

description: Gilles de Bins, known as Binchois, was one of the leading figures of the Burgundian School. A singer and composer in the service of the Burgundian court, he developed a refined art of courtly song, marked by melodic clarity, elegant lines and restrained expressiveness. His sacred music also demonstrates the contrapuntal mastery of musicians of his time. Alongside Dufay, he helped shape the musical taste of 15th-century European courts.

name: Hildegarde de Bingen
description: Hildegard of Bingen was an extraordinary figure of the 12th century: a Benedictine abbess, visionary author, theologian, naturalist and composer. Leading communities of women along the Rhine, she created a body of work in which poetry, symbolic thought and music form an indivisible whole. Her surviving musical corpus comprises around 77 liturgical chants, most with texts written by Hildegard herself, as well as the morality play Ordo Virtutum. Her melodies, often unusually wide-ranging and richly ornamented, extend beyond the customary contours of chant in her time. Their singularity also lies in the way the vocal line follows the imagery and movement of the text.

description: Born in Lucca into a family of musicians, Luigi Boccherini was a virtuoso cellist and composer. After periods in Vienna and Paris, he settled in Spain in the service of the Infante Don Luis, and later worked for several European patrons. He made a major contribution to the development of chamber music, especially the string quintet with two cellos, a formation whose possibilities he explored with great inventiveness. His instrumental writing is distinguished by elegant lines, rich dialogue between voices and an especially expressive role for the cello.

name: Anthony Braxton
description: Anthony Braxton is a saxophonist, improviser, educator and composer. Emerging from Chicago's experimental scene, he became involved with the Association for the Advancement of Creative Musicians (AACM), which championed aesthetic and institutional autonomy for African American musicians. His work reaches far beyond the categories of jazz: he has developed an immense system of compositions, graphic languages, diagrams and improvised structures. The Ghost Trance Music series, his orchestral compositions and his operatic cycles embody a mode of thought that is both systematic and open, closely interweaving improvisation, notation and collaboration.

description: William Byrd was one of the greatest English composers of the Renaissance. Despite the confessional tensions of Elizabethan England, he wrote for both Anglican institutions and clandestine Catholic communities. His output spans sacred and secular vocal music, keyboard works and consort music. He combined exceptional contrapuntal learning with an often sombre expressiveness, especially evident in his Latin motets and keyboard pieces.

description: Francesca Caccini, known as la Cecchina, was a composer, singer and instrumentalist at the Medici court in Florence. The daughter of Giulio Caccini, she became one of the most remarkable musicians of her time and took an active part in the invention of Baroque music theatre. Her opera La liberazione di Ruggiero dall'isola d'Alcina, premiered in 1625, is the earliest known opera composed by a woman. Her career reveals the real, though often obscured, place of women in court musical institutions.

name: John Cage
description: John Cage studied, among others, with [[schoenberg|Arnold Schoenberg]], but soon moved away from traditional ideas of composition. From the 1940s onwards, he explored percussion, prepared instruments, chance operations inspired by the I Ching and indeterminacy. His celebrated 4′33″ shifts attention away from the musical object towards listening to the sounds present in a given situation. Close to New York's avant-garde artists, he collaborated with choreographers such as Merce Cunningham and profoundly influenced visual art, performance and experimental practice. Rather than defining what music is, his work questions the very conditions of listening.

His style combines the Italian contrapuntal tradition with a dramatic approach shaped by [[gluck|Gluck]] and French opera. His operas, especially Médée, are admired for their tension and demanding vocal writing. He composed almost exclusively for the piano, yet profoundly renewed its language: virtuosity became expression, dance forms turned into poetic structures, and harmony ventured into new colours. His mazurkas and polonaises maintain a complex relationship with the rhythms and memories of his homeland. His relationship with George Sand marked a long period of creativity, especially at Nohant. His music permanently reshaped the technique and poetry of piano writing.

Trained at the Conservatorio di Santa Maria di Loreto, he quickly found success in Naples before working in several European cities, notably St Petersburg and Vienna. His virtuosity helped establish the piano as a central instrument of modern musical life. His sonatas explore the range, power and technical possibilities of the new instrument, and their inventiveness was admired by [[beethoven|Beethoven]]. His language transformed harmony, form and orchestration through modes, non-functional chords, timbre and resonance. Though often associated with Impressionism, he rejected the label. Against conventions that prized vocal virtuosity for its own sake, he advocated a more continuous dramaturgy in which overture, chorus, dance and recitative contributed to the unity of the drama. description: Japanese trumpeter Toshinori Kondo developed a practice at the intersection of free jazz, improvisation and electronics. Live processing transforms the trumpet's timbre into textures approaching synthesis. His collaborations with Brötzmann, Bill Laswell and other musicians connect experimental scenes in Japan, Europe and the United States.

name: Helmut Lachenmann
description: Helmut Lachenmann studied in Stuttgart and later with Luigi Nono in Venice. He developed what he called instrumental concrete music: rather than treating instruments simply as producers of notes, he explores the gestures, friction, breath, resistance and noise through which sound becomes possible. This approach transforms listening and reveals the physical and social conditions of musical practice. Demanding of performers and audiences alike, his work does not seek novelty for its own sake; it questions perceptual habits and conventions inherited from the concert tradition.

description: Florentine composer, organist and poet Francesco Landini was the most celebrated figure of the Italian Trecento. His two- and three-part ballate combine melodic suppleness, contrapuntal refinement and courtly poetry. His music is essential to understanding the flowering of Italian secular music before the Renaissance.

description: György Ligeti lived through several of the major transformations in music during the second half of the 20th century. After fleeing Hungary in 1956, he joined the electronic music studios in Cologne, then developed an instrumental language based on sound masses, micropolyphony and transformations of texture. His music eludes schools and serial orthodoxies. He also explored polyrhythms, absurd mechanisms and perceptual illusions.

description: American composer Alvin Lucier explored acoustic phenomena, resonance, brain waves and the physical properties of spaces. His work lies at the intersection of experimental music, installation and sound art. Rather than composing traditional musical objects, he created situations in which sound reveals phenomena that normally remain imperceptible. description: Witold Lutosławski was one of the major Polish composers of the 20th century. His style evolved from neoclassicism towards a personal language based on controlled aleatory, mobile textures and exceptional orchestral command. He devised systems in which performers enjoy rhythmic freedom within a carefully structured framework. His orchestral and concertante works rank among the great achievements of post-war contemporary music.

name: Guillaume de Machaut
description: As much a poet as a musician, Guillaume de Machaut served as secretary and cleric to powerful lords, notably John of Luxembourg, King of Bohemia, and later the court of Navarre. His work, carefully transmitted in often richly illuminated manuscripts, offers one of the earliest authorial bodies of music in Europe. He wrote in the fixed forms — ballade, rondeau and virelai — as well as the motet and liturgical music. His Messe de Nostre Dame is one of the earliest complete polyphonic mass cycles attributed to a single composer. His art combines contrapuntal architecture, formal virtuosity and an intense relationship between poetry and music.

His five books of viol pieces form a vast repertoire documenting the evolution of French chamber music under Louis XIV and the Regency.

His extensive catalogue spans symphonies, operas, concertos and chamber music, in a modern style that is mobile and luminous.

He wrote madrigals, operas, sacred music and ballets. L'Orfeo (1607) is among the earliest great surviving operas. In his later books of madrigals, voice, instrument and basso continuo become the actors in miniature dramas of unprecedented intensity.

After years in the service of the Archbishop of Salzburg, he settled in Vienna as an independent musician, an audacious and precarious position. He composed in almost every genre of his time: opera, symphony, concerto, chamber music, serenade and sacred music. His music theatre observes social and psychological relationships with exceptional subtlety, while his instrumental music combines formal balance and intensity. His final opera, The Magic Flute, and the unfinished Requiem belong to the last months of his life.

His reputation was immense: music printing helped spread his masses, motets and chansons throughout Europe. description: Jean-Philippe Rameau was a major composer of French opera and an influential theorist. He renewed music theatre through his tragédies en musique and opéras-ballets. His Traité de l'harmonie (1722) systematised a theory of the fundamental bass that had a lasting impact on Western music theory.

name: Steve Reich
description: Steve Reich developed a music based on repetition, phasing and the attentive listening to processes. His early experiments with magnetic tape led to instrumental works in which patterns gradually shift, revealing complex perceptual structures. He later integrated influences from African, Balinese and Hebrew music. His work profoundly influenced contemporary music, dance and audiovisual art.

name: Silvestre Revueltas
description: Violoniste et compositeur mexicain, Revueltas mêle rythmes populaires, fanfares, dissonances et superpositions de plans dans une écriture orchestrale d'une grande vitalité. Sa carrière brève est interrompue à quarante ans. Sa musique pour le cinéma et ses poèmes symphoniques témoignent d'une modernité profondément ancrée dans la vie urbaine mexicaine.

name: Terry Riley
description: Terry Riley est l'un des fondateurs du minimalisme américain. Son travail sur la répétition, les cycles, les boucles de bande et l'improvisation transforme radicalement les conceptions de la forme musicale dans les années 1960. In C, partition ouverte pour ensemble, devient une œuvre emblématique de cette esthétique. Riley est également marqué par la musique classique indienne, notamment par son étude du chant avec Pandit Pran Nath, qui infléchit profondément son rapport au temps et à la modalité.

name: Jean-Claude Risset
description: Compositeur et chercheur français, Risset est un pionnier de la synthèse numérique du son. Ses travaux aux laboratoires Bell et à l'Ircam éclairent les illusions auditives, les sons paradoxaux et les transformations spectrales. Il fait de l'informatique un instrument de pensée musicale, et non un simple outil de production.

name: Amadeo Roldán
description: Compositeur et violoniste cubain, Roldán intègre dans l'orchestre symphonique les percussions et les rythmes afro-cubains, ouvrant un champ nouveau pour la composition du XXe siècle. Associée au mouvement afrocubanista, sa musique transforme les matériaux populaires en structures modernistes sans les réduire au pittoresque.

Obertura sobre temas cubanos

name: Keith Rowe
description: Guitariste britannique, membre fondateur d'AMM, Rowe transforme la guitare en surface de résonance et de bruit. Posée à plat, préparée et reliée à des dispositifs électroniques, elle explore feedbacks, textures et écoute collective. Son influence sur l'improvisation et l'électronique expérimentale est considérable.

name: Pierre de La Rue
description: Pierre de La Rue est l'un des grands représentants de la génération franco-flamande qui succède à Josquin. Actif à la cour des Habsbourg, il développe une polyphonie dense et souvent sombre, où les voix graves structurent l'ensemble. Ses messes, motets et chansons comptent parmi les réalisations majeures de la Renaissance septentrionale.

name: Frederic Rzewski
description: Frederic Rzewski est un pianiste et compositeur américain dont l'œuvre associe virtuosité, improvisation, engagement politique et mémoire des luttes sociales. Cofondateur de l'ensemble Musica Elettronica Viva, il explore les formes ouvertes et l'improvisation collective avant de développer un vaste catalogue pour piano et ensemble. The People United Will Never Be Defeated! est l'un des grands cycles de variations du répertoire pianistique contemporain.

name: Kaija Saariaho
description: Kaija Saariaho étudie à Helsinki, Fribourg et à l'IRCAM à Paris, où elle approfondit les relations entre acoustique, informatique musicale et écriture instrumentale. Associée à la génération spectrale, elle ne se limite pas à une école : elle façonne des univers sonores où timbre, texture, électronique et dramaturgie se répondent. Ses opéras lui apportent une reconnaissance internationale, en particulier L'Amour de loin, créé au Festival de Salzbourg en 2000. Son œuvre explore fréquemment des états de transformation, la fragilité des voix et les correspondances entre phénomènes naturels et expériences intérieures.

name: Joseph Bologne de Saint-Georges
description: Né en Guadeloupe, Joseph Bologne de Saint-Georges est violoniste, compositeur, chef d'orchestre et escrimeur. Fils de Georges de Bologne de Saint-Georges et de Nanon, femme réduite en esclavage, il est envoyé en France où il reçoit une éducation aristocratique et développe une carrière exceptionnelle malgré les discriminations raciales de son époque. Il devient premier violon du Concert des Amateurs, puis dirige le Concert de la Loge Olympique, ensemble associé à la création des symphonies parisiennes de Haydn. Son œuvre comprend des concertos pour violon, des symphonies concertantes, des quatuors et des opéras.

name: Antonio Salieri
description: Né à Legnago, en Vénétie, Antonio Salieri se forme à Venise avant de s'établir à Vienne, où il devient l'un des musiciens les plus influents de la cour impériale. Compositeur d'opéras, chef et pédagogue, il occupe une place institutionnelle majeure dans la vie musicale européenne. Son activité pédagogique le met en relation avec plusieurs générations de musiciens, parmi lesquels [[beethoven|Beethoven]], [[schubert|Schubert]] et Liszt. Son œuvre lyrique circule entre les traditions italienne et française. Sa postérité populaire a été déformée par le récit romanesque d'une rivalité meurtrière avec Mozart : aucun élément historique sérieux ne permet de lui attribuer l'empoisonnement de son confrère.

description: Troisième membre de la trinité carnatique, Syama Sastri laisse une œuvre moins abondante mais d'une grande densité musicale. Ses compositions sont réputées pour leurs talas complexes. Ses kritis adressés à la déesse Kamakshi associent intensité dévotionnelle, virtuosité rythmique et profondeur mélodique.

name: Erik Satie
description: Erik Satie occupe une place singulière dans la modernité musicale française. Refusant les conventions du romantisme tardif et les ambitions monumentales, il développe une esthétique de l'économie, de l'ironie et de la répétition, qui influencera aussi bien les avant-gardes que la musique minimaliste. Ses partitions, souvent accompagnées d'indications textuelles insolites, mettent en crise les habitudes d'écoute et la frontière entre musique savante, cabaret et geste conceptuel.

name: Domenico Scarlatti
description: Installé au service des cours portugaise puis espagnole, Scarlatti compose 555 sonates pour clavier qui constituent un corpus exceptionnel. Nourries de rythmes ibériques, de croisements de mains et de dissonances, ces pièces brèves élargissent les possibilités du clavier et annoncent certains traits du langage classique.

description: Giacinto Scelsi traverse une longue crise personnelle et artistique avant de développer, à partir des années 1950, un langage radicalement singulier. Plutôt que de construire la musique par thèmes et développements, il concentre l'écoute sur la matière interne d'un son : battements, micro-intervalles, harmoniques, souffle et transformations imperceptibles. Il travaille avec des interprètes capables de réaliser ses intuitions, notamment en improvisant au piano puis en faisant transcrire et élaborer ces improvisations. Son œuvre, longtemps marginale, est aujourd'hui reconnue comme une contribution majeure à l'exploration du timbre et de la perception.

name: Pierre Schaeffer
description: Ingénieur, chercheur, écrivain et compositeur, Pierre Schaeffer est le fondateur de la musique concrète. À partir de 1948, il expérimente l'enregistrement, le montage, la boucle et la transformation des sons fixés, rompant avec l'idée que la musique doit nécessairement être produite par des instruments traditionnels. Sa réflexion sur l'objet sonore, l'écoute réduite et la morphologie du son constitue un socle théorique essentiel pour les musiques électroacoustiques.

Ses sonates et ballets associent virtuosité, danses et contrastes expressifs. Il figure parmi les premiers grands compositeurs de musique instrumentale de l'espace germanique.

name: Arnold Schönberg
description: Arnold Schönberg commence comme compositeur postromantique à Vienne et Berlin avant de devenir l'une des figures décisives de la modernité musicale. Autodidacte en grande partie, pédagogue influent, il traverse une période d'expérimentation atonale puis élabore la méthode de composition avec douze sons, souvent appelée dodécaphonisme. Son parcours ne se réduit pas à une rupture théorique : l'expressionnisme de ses œuvres, leur rapport à la voix et leur densité contrapuntique témoignent d'une recherche dramatique continue. Contraint à l'exil par le nazisme en raison de ses origines juives, il s'installe aux États-Unis en 1933.

description: Clara Wieck, devenue Clara Schumann par son mariage avec Robert Schumann, est l'une des pianistes les plus célèbres du XIXe siècle. Formée très tôt par son père Friedrich Wieck, elle mène une carrière internationale de virtuose, compose dès l'enfance et contribue ensuite à faire connaître la musique de son mari et celle de Johannes Brahms, avec lequel elle entretient une relation artistique et personnelle complexe. Les contraintes de la vie familiale et d'une carrière de concertiste limitent progressivement son activité de compositrice, mais ses œuvres révèlent une maîtrise remarquable du piano, de la forme et de l'écriture de chambre.

Son écriture explore sons harmoniques, bruits de clés et frottements. Son théâtre musical déconstruit les formes lyriques au profit d'une dramaturgie du silence, de l'écoute et de l'apparition.

Son Quatuor à cordes de 1931 est l'une des œuvres les plus radicales de la musique américaine de son temps. Elle se consacre ensuite à la collecte et à l'édition de chants populaires.

description: Ravi Shankar est l'un des grands maîtres du sitar et une figure essentielle de la diffusion internationale de la musique classique de l'Inde du Nord. Formé auprès d'Allauddin Khan, il développe une carrière de concertiste, de pédagogue et de compositeur. Ses collaborations avec Yehudi Menuhin et George Harrison contribuent à faire connaître le raga au-delà de son contexte traditionnel. Son concept de spectromorphologie décrit les formes et transformations du son dans le temps et fournit un vocabulaire d'analyse de l'écoute électroacoustique. Son œuvre pour instruments à clavier est particulièrement remarquable : sonates, pièces de caractère et concertos pour deux orgues témoignent d'une synthèse entre traditions ibériques, style galant et formes européennes nouvelles. Sa carrière le conduit à Paris, Londres et Moscou. Ses études, sonates et variations associent clarté formelle, élégance classique et idiomatisme instrumental. Il joue un rôle décisif dans la constitution de l'école de Mannheim, orchestre célèbre pour sa précision, sa discipline collective et ses effets dynamiques. Ses symphonies contribuent à stabiliser une forme en plusieurs mouvements et à développer des procédés orchestraux devenus emblématiques du classicisme, tels que les crescendos progressifs, les fusées mélodiques et les contrastes de dynamique. name: Barbara Strozzi
description: Barbara Strozzi grandit dans le milieu intellectuel et artistique de Venise. Chanteuse et compositrice, elle est liée à l'Accademia degli Unisoni, cercle fondé par son père adoptif Giulio Strozzi, où la musique et la discussion littéraire se rencontrent. Ses cantates explorent les affects amoureux avec une grande liberté rhétorique : récitatifs expressifs, ariosos, airs virtuoses et contrastes dramatiques. Sa production imprimée, abondante et largement conservée, permet de mesurer une voix d'autrice particulièrement affirmée dans le Seicento.

Ses opéras fondés sur des sujets mythiques ou politiques interrogent violence, rédemption et contradictions de la société moderne.

Il conçoit la musique comme une architecture de masses, de densités et de trajectoires plutôt que comme un développement mélodique traditionnel. Son intérêt pour les nouvelles technologies et les sons non instrumentaux en fait une figure fondatrice de la musique électroacoustique. Des œuvres comme Ionisation et Déserts bouleversent les frontières entre bruit, timbre et composition.

name: Tomás Luis de Victoria
description: Tomás Luis de Victoria est le plus célèbre compositeur espagnol de la Renaissance tardive. Prêtre, il étudie et travaille longtemps à Rome avant de revenir à Madrid. Sa musique exclusivement sacrée se distingue par une intensité contemplative, une écriture vocale limpide et une grande maîtrise des contrastes. Le Officium Defunctorum, publié en 1605, est l'un des chefs-d'œuvre de la musique funèbre de la Renaissance et l'aboutissement de son art.

Il y compose et dirige une grande partie de sa musique vocale et instrumentale. Son catalogue comprend plusieurs centaines de concertos, mais aussi des opéras, des cantates, des oratorios et de la musique sacrée. Il donne au concerto une énergie théâtrale fondée sur l'alternance du tutti et du soliste, les ritournelles, les contrastes de texture et une invention mélodique immédiatement reconnaissable.

name: Richard Wagner
description: Richard Wagner construit une œuvre lyrique qui transforme profondément le rapport entre musique, poésie, scène et mythe. Après des débuts marqués par l'opéra romantique allemand, il développe le concept de drame musical et défend l'idée d'une œuvre d'art totale. L'harmonie chromatique de Tristan und Isolde pousse la tonalité vers ses limites, tandis que le cycle de L'Anneau du Nibelung déploie sur quatre soirées une vaste dramaturgie mythologique. Son influence sur la musique et la mise en scène est immense, mais son antisémitisme virulent et ses écrits politiques imposent de ne pas dissocier l'étude de son œuvre de son contexte idéologique.

name: Carl Maria von Weber
description: Carl Maria von Weber est l'une des figures fondatrices de l'opéra romantique allemand. Issu d'une famille liée au théâtre itinérant, il grandit dans un environnement où la musique et la scène sont étroitement mêlées. Chef d'orchestre, pianiste et compositeur, il dirige notamment les théâtres de Prague puis de Dresde, où il défend un répertoire allemand. Der Freischütz, créé en 1821, connaît un succès considérable grâce à son univers fantastique, à ses couleurs orchestrales et à son ancrage dans les légendes populaires. Weber renouvelle l'orchestration et le traitement du surnaturel au théâtre, ouvrant une voie qui influencera Wagner.

Après des œuvres de jeunesse encore marquées par le postromantisme, il adopte l'atonalité puis la technique dodécaphonique. Son langage se caractérise par une extrême concentration, une économie de moyens et une attention minutieuse au timbre, à la durée et au silence. Son influence sur le sérialisme d'après-guerre est considérable.
